scope: Statically reconstructed payload and resources, not automatic decryption during original archive scanning. Expected findings include capabilities; these are not 15 complete attack-chain proofs.

items.note: Detects locale comparison cluster and hostname sandbox test; does not prove every exit branch or every sandbox probe.
Detects kill/hosts combinations, a privileged container mounting writable host sudoers near a passwordless grant, and a resolver replacement command. Does not claim these alternatives all execute.

items.item: SSH, registry, Git, dotenv and browser credentials
items.note: Browser collection and multi-store behavior detected; individual store findings identify targets, not proof of successful theft.

items.item: Claude, Codex, Gemini and Copilot credentials
items.note: Target coverage only. qk assembles auth-file paths and qn reads them; the monolithic flow graph is truncated, so findings do not prove each read-to-exfil path.

items.item: AWS, GCP, Azure, Vault and Kubernetes secrets
items.note: Capability and target coverage; endpoint references alone are not credential theft verdicts.
Hostile archive correlation combines runner identity and secret records with the embedded procfs memory dumper.
Detects public repository options and content commit PUT body. Source audit confirms encrypted envelope; findings do not prove end-to-end dataflow or rely on project-utils/random repository names.

Suspicious cooccurrence: token string assembly, content commits and commit search. Does not prove hardcoded-key encryption or token reuse from these matches alone; no dependency on AutoSyncComplete marker.
Generic HTTPS POST/JSON capability only. Ei sends envelope data, Fc configures aiarmor.website:443/v1/api; source audit establishes destination, not the generic POST finding.

items.item: npm loader insertion and patch republish
items.note: Gyp command generation with version increment is suspicious. npm maintainer search and GitHub commit API cooccurrence is a neutral capability, not proof of propagation.
Suspicious repack/publish combinations, not ordinary registry publishing alone.

items.item: Fake CodeQL, agent files, GitHub and GitLab injection
items.note: Workflow export behavior plus commit and startup-file capabilities. Commit-author/message copying and the Windows loader path are audited source details, not separately classified behaviors.
Self-file read plus scp stdin transfer, SSH Bash launch and disabled host checking; no assumed interprocedural byte flow.

items.item: Token rejection wiper and installed monitor
items.note: Archive correlation connects HTTP 401/403 eval branch, token check and destructive handler. 45-second interval and 48-hour TTL verified in source, not fixed in signature.

items.item: Signed GitHub dead-drop Python execution and persistence
items.note: Existing hostile signed-commit C2 detection; systemd and launchd persistence capabilities. One-hour cadence and msync-3f7a marker verified without becoming signature requirements.

validation: make validate: all repository suites pass (779 hostile, 1817 benign, 176 does-nothing, plus all specialized suites)

atomscan.note: Scans use local working traits. Rule IDs are deduplicated across archive rollups and exact source slices. Original archive does not automatically expose the encrypted payload.

hopper: Original SHA-256 remains in bad; prior relabel returned already-correct noop.
